entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 2 (its HST coordinates, 12:50:57.264 +41:07:23.13); SIMBAD holds that position, from 2019MNRAS.484L..24S, SIMBAD basic row main_id = [SVF2019] NGC 4736-1: J2000 position; Gaia cannot see the star. Distance: Placed in M94 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 4,337,391 pc (src/objects/m94-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 4,337,106 pc, inclination 31.77 deg, line of nodes 105 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 43495: distance modulus 28.186 ± 0.039 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94) (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94): 4337391 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star. Proper motion: basic row main_id = [SVF2019] NGC 4736-1 measures no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 4,337,391 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 20,561 km/s across the sky). Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity of M94, the star's galaxy, from 1999PASP..111..438F; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 183 +/- 74 solar radii from Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 3.1: log(L_bol/L_sun) = 6.5 +/- 0.2 (at the paper's distance modulus of M94, 28.31) and T = 18 +/- 3 kK, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolution B3, Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788); the paper prints no radius, and no measurement of this star's size exists (https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.05277). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 18000 +/- 3000 K from Solovyeva et al. (2019), MNRAS 484, L24, section 3.1: photosphere temperature T = 18 +/- 3 kK, estimated from the strengths of its He I and Fe II lines.

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 18,000 K, because no archive holds a spectrum of this star (stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: the star is placed by a catalogue row, so no Gaia DR3 source is read for it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #aec4ff. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: the star is placed by a catalogue row, so no Gaia DR3 source is read for it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Reeve & Howarth (2016), MNRAS 456, 1294 compute from non-LTE TLUSTY B-star model atmospheres for the Bessell V band at 18,000 K and log g 2.15 (u1 0.290, u2 0.271): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Surface gravity
entries.finding: Unmeasured, bounded: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Clark et al. (2012), A&A 541, A145, table 4 (the model gravities of the four Galactic early-B hypergiants it analyses, at 13.7 to 18.1 kK, stars it finds intermediate between B supergiants and luminous blue variables) gives the class's range, log g 1.7 to 2.38. Across log g 2 to 2.35, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 3.3% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 2.15, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 2.15 is a display choice, not a measurement.
